author: Andrew Messenger
description:
As minister says process needs to be ‘streamlined’, Greens and Lock the Gate say the legislation is ‘corrupt’ and tears up environmental protections

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Queenslanders’ right to object to mining projects – including coal – would be “gutted” by new legislation that would ban opponents from being heard in court without the minister’s approval and then only if they owned a property within a 125km radius of the project.

The Greens have called the move “corrupt” and community action group Lock the Gate Alliance said the state’s LNP government was “tearing up democratic and environmental protections just to make life easier for mining companies”.
title: Queenslanders’ rights to oppose mining projects ‘gutted’ by new laws, activists say

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
description:
Bears came through bedroom window and swiped tent at campground, causing scratch marks and puncture wound

A black bear burst through a Colorado teenage girl’s window and scratched her, days after a bear also bit a camper in the state, according to wildlife officials.

On Friday, a woman at a campground in south-west Colorado heard a growl and felt something hit her outdoors tent, according to a news release.

Continue reading...
title: Sleeping teen and camper wounded as Colorado bear attacks reach record high

author: Patrick Butler Social policy editor
description:
More than a million people have left work to look after loved ones in the past two years, Carers UK says

About 1,500 Britons a day are quitting their jobs to become unpaid carers, as they try to balance their vulnerable relatives’ growing care needs with declining access to state-funded social care services.

Research estimates that more than a million people have left the workplace to look after ageing, ill and disabled loved ones in the past two years, highlighting the social challenges caused by UK’s rapidly changing demographic profile.

Continue reading...
title: About 1,500 Britons a day quitting their jobs to become unpaid carers

author: Yassin El-Moudden
description:
PC Mason O’Connor dismissed following Panorama film showing misogyny and racism at London police station

A 13th serving Metropolitan police officer has been dismissed in relation to an undercover BBC investigation into misogyny and racism at Charing Cross police station.

PC Mason O’Connor was found to have committed discreditable conduct and breached professional behaviour standards, linked to a comment he made towards a female colleague, according to the Met.

Continue reading...
title: Thirteenth Met police officer sacked after undercover BBC investigation

author: Guardian moderators (now); Shrai Popat, David Smith, Alice Speri, Joseph Gedeon and Rachel Leingang (later)
description:
Who are the Democrats running in the midterms, and where do they stand? Our political reporters will be hosting a series of conversations on the critical issues ahead of November. First up: the state of the Democrats, the party’s moderate and leftwing candidates and key races to watch. Drop your questions and join us live at 12pm (EDT) on 16 September

Sign up or sign in to post a question

We’re less than two months from the midterm elections that could have an outsized impact on the future of the United States.

With the primaries wrapped, our reporting team is fanned out across the country to tell the stories behind the horse race, from Washington to the Midwest and along the West Coast.
title: Reader Q&A: how united are the Democrats ahead of the midterms? Post your questions now

author: Anna Betts
description:
Financier refused to comply with subpoenas seeking his testimony for the investigation into the late sex offender

The House oversight committee voted unanimously Tuesday to recommend that the House of Representatives hold Leon Black, the billionaire financier, in contempt of Congress, after he refused to comply with subpoenas seeking his testimony and nondisclosure agreements (NDAs) sought by the panel as part of its investigation into Jeffrey Epstein. Black contends the subpoenas are “invalid” and he is suing to block them.

“Subpoenas are not suggestions; they carry the force of law and require full compliance” the representative James Comer, who chairs the committee, said in the chamber on Tuesday afternoon before the voting began. “Mr Black’s testimony is crucial to our investigation because he maintained a close personal relati
title: House committee recommends Leon Black be held in contempt of Congress over Epstein inquiry subpoenas

author: Luca Ittimani and Caitlin Cassidy
description:
Proposals revealed as senior personnel from OpenAI, the creator of ChatGPT, met with Albanese ministers

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Albanese government is considering giving AI companies access to Australian creatives’ works by default as its pursues a compromise with American tech giants.

The proposals were revealed as senior personnel from OpenAI, the creator of ChatGPT, met with Labor ministers and warned Australia’s copyright laws were preventing the company training models locally.
title: Pocock says Labor easing copyright protections for AI datacentre investment would throw creatives ‘under the bus’

author: Martin Farrer
description:
Follow the day’s news live

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

The head of One Nation in New South Wales has fronted a rally opposing “abortion up to birth” ahead of an expected vote in the upper house on Libertarian member John Ruddick’s bill to ban
title: Australia politics live: Lambie blasts ‘dangerous’ and ‘delusional’ Hanson; Marles ‘comforted’ by calls for AI pause

author: David Smith in Washington
description:
Leftwing senator and far-right strategist rail against tech oligarchs but offer competing visions on Chinese ‘cold war’

The progressive senator Bernie Sanders and rightwing strategist Steve Bannon have called for restrictions on artificial intelligence (AI) but offered competing visions for what they termed a “cold war” with China.

Speaking at the “Pro-Human Assembly” in Washington on Tuesday, the ideological adversaries were united in warning of the potential dangers of AI and demanding stringent guardrails against Silicon Valley’s “oligarchs”.

Continue reading...
title: Bernie Sanders and Steve Bannon call for curbs on AI at ‘pro-human’ summit

author: Alexandra Topping, Political correspondent
description:
Employers will have to hold face-to-face meetings with staff who ask about shift changes under government reforms

Company bosses will have to sit down with workers who request flexible working and justify their reasons for any refusals under new rights announced by Louise Haigh on Tuesday.

The first secretary of state told the TUC conference that employers would have to “properly consider” requests for flexibility and offer a face-to-face meeting under new rights for workers.

Continue reading...
title: British bosses to be forced to meet with employees who request flexible working

author: Cecilia Nowell
description:
Nathaniel James McGuire faces maximum sentence of life in prison after guilty plea over September 2024 bombing

A California man has pleaded guilty to charges that he detonated a bomb at a Santa Maria courthouse in 2024 in retaliation for law enforcement officers seizing his firearms earlier that year.

In September 2024, Nathaniel James McGuire, 22, of Santa Barbara county threw a backpack containing an explosive device into the courthouse before exiting the building to retrieve two long guns and 10 molotov cocktails from his car.

Continue reading...
title: Man admits to bombing California courthouse in retaliation for seized guns

author: Leyland Cecco in Toronto and Jennifer Rankin in Strasbourg
description:
Prime minister speaks of strengthening Canada’s economic and political ties to Europe at Canada Investment Summit

Mark Carney said Canada will pursue a “unique security and economic alliance” with Europe as he positions his country as a base to build in the “new global economic order”.

Speaking to investors, company executives and government ministers at the inaugural Canada Investment Summit on Tuesday, the prime minister pitched Canada as a “safe harbour” and lucrative home for foreign capital as his government looks to reduce its reliance on trade with the United States.

Continue reading...
title: Carney says Canada will pursue ‘unique economic alliance’ with EU amid US trade spat

author: Geneva Abdul
description:
Nearly half of ethnic minority respondents in a poll say they have faced prejudice over the past year

Many Britons feel inequality is worsening and that discrimination has become more common, according to a thinktank study.

The report by British Future has found that people across ethnic groups believe racial equality is worsening in Britain. One in six people are from ethnic minority backgrounds.

Continue reading...
title: People from ethnic groups feel racial equality is worsening, UK study shows

author: David Conn
description:
Decision not to pause proceedings means £18m report does not engage with concerns over former nurse’s conviction

Just two months before Lady Justice Kathryn Thirlwall opened her inquiry into events at the Countess of Chester hospital and the crimes of Lucy Letby, a report by Chris Henley KC was published into the “atrocious” wrongful conviction of Andrew Malkinson for rape.

Henley prefaced that report with a plea for the legal establishment to recognise that the criminal courts produce miscarriages of justice. Right up to top judges in the court of appeal, Henley wrote, the system has “a deep-seated … cultural reluctance” to accept it “will on occasion make mistakes” and that “entirely innocent defendants will sometimes be convicted”.
title: Thirlwall inquiry has left biggest questions around the Letby case unanswered

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
Karl Rove, a respected GOP consultant, further said he would vote for ‘bigot’ Bo French’s Democratic opponent after post

A senior Republican has called a party colleague running for office in Texas “a bigot” over a racist social media post attacking college football fans – and said he is so outraged by the comments that he will vote for the candidate’s Democratic rival.

Karl Rove, who was former president George W Bush’s longtime political adviser and is a respected Republican consultant in Texas, told a private event in Austin on Sunday that he could not support Bo French’s candidacy for a seat on the state’s railroad commission, the Texas Tribune reported.

Continue reading...
title: Republicans criticize racist social media post by Texas member running for office

author: Chris Stein in Washington
description:
Congressman says defense secretary repeatedly violated constitution through his handling of Iran war

Republican congressman Thomas Massie on Tuesday proposed impeaching Pete Hegseth, saying the defense secretary had repeatedly violated the constitution through his handling of war with Iran and the deaths of civilians in conflicts worldwide.

The proposal by Massie, an iconoclastic lawmaker who lost his primary earlier this year after Donald Trump and Hegseth urged voters to oppose him, may put House Republicans in a bind just weeks before the 3 November midterm elections, where they are defending their control of Congress.

Continue reading...
title: Republican Thomas Massie proposes impeaching Pete Hegseth over Iran war

author: Maya Yang
description:
Jayden Williams of Stockbridge alleged to have made inappropriate texts to teen and using city funds improperly

  • US politics live – latest updates

City leaders in a suburb outside Atlanta have voted to remove the youngest mayor in their community’s history amid allegations of questionable spending of municipal funds and inappropriate communications with an 18-year-old high school student.

Over the weekend, the Stockbridge, Georgia, city council voted to remove Jayden Williams, 23, from office after an hours-long hearing into a
title: Georgia city removes 23-year-old mayor after sexting and municipal funds scandal

author: Ariana Baio
description:
Senators question FBI chief on move to cut restrictions on agent applicants who have engaged in bestiality

  • US politics live – latest updates

FBI director Kash Patel defended his agency’s decision to roll back restrictions on agent applicants who have previously engaged in bestiality, arguing the FBI “did not want to punish victims of bestiality” by automatically disqualifying them.

The unusual topic of bestiality emerged during a Senate judiciary committee oversight hearing on Tuesday after Democrat Dick Durbin and Republican John Kennedy questioned Patel’s decision to remove barriers that previously prevented applicants who engaged in prostitut
title: Kash Patel defends FBI hiring policy on applicants who have engaged in bestiality

author: Andrew Roth and Chris Stein in Washington
description:
Proponents say sanctions would help Ukraine, but some Democrats say Trump shouldn’t have more tariff authority

  • US politics live – latest updates

A bill co-authored by Lindsey Graham, the South Carolina senator who died earlier this year, that would give Donald Trump broad authority to tariff Russia and its trading partners will be put forward for a vote this week in a high-stakes legislative battle that could provide new sanctioning authority to the US president at a crucial moment in Russia’s war against Ukraine.

The bill is facing considerable pushback not only from Ukraine-sceptic
title: US lawmakers spar over bill giving Trump more power to sanction Russia

author: Sarah Martin Senior correspondent
description:
Exclusive: Lee Hanson also appears to be regularly campaigning for party during work hours, social media shows

  • Listen to Guardian Australia’s podcast The Populist here

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Pauline Hanson’s daughter, Lee Hanson, has been working in Tasmania as a senior adviser to a New South Wales One Nation senator without the required ministerial approval, Guardian Australia can reveal.

Under work base arrangements that apply to the staff of all MPs, a personal adviser such as Hanson can only be allowed to work in a location other than Canberra or the parliamentarian’s home base with app
title: Pauline Hanson’s daughter Lee working for a NSW One Nation senator remotely from Tasmania without ministerial approval

author: Henry Belot
description:
Exclusive: Correspondence requests state MP Melissa Horne to lobby on NextDC’s behalf – but contains alleged AI-created errors

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Victorian jobs minister has accused one of Australia’s largest datacentre companies of using artificial intelligence while requesting she lobby her colleague to approve a massive expansion of its “hyperscale AI factory”.

Correspondence between Victorian cabinet minister Melissa Horne and the chief executive of ASX-listed company NextDC, Craig Scroggie, reveals increasing sensitivity to community concerns about datacentres before the state election.
title: Datacentre giant accused of using AI while lobbying for Victorian minister’s support for hyperscale factory

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
Disbanding of department in Trinidad comes after arrest of a resident for posting about issues with local water supply

A police department in Texas that arrested a local resident for complaining on social media about their city’s contaminated water supply has been ordered closed after failing to prove it provided any benefit to the community.

State officials stepped in to investigate after Jennifer Combs spent a night in jail in May after a post appeared on her Facebook page suggesting people were hospitalized by bacteria in the water pipes of Trinidad, a municipality in Henderson county about 75 miles south-east of Dallas.

Continue reading...
title: Texas police department ordered closed for failing to provide any benefit to community

author: Jamie Grierson
description:
Lady Justice Thirlwall’s wide-ranging inquiry calls on NHS England to implement 14 changes by March next year

  • Lucy Letby public inquiry report published – latest updates

Lady Justice Thirlwall has published the report on the findings of her inquiry into events at the Countess of Chester hospital involving the actions of former neonatal nurse Lucy Letby, who was convicted over the murder and attempted murder of multiple babies.

Here we take a look at the report and its findings.

Continue reading...
title: Thirlwall report: what did it say about Lucy Letby case and what does it recommend?

author: Yohannes Lowe
description:
Long-awaited Thrilwall inquiry has examined how the former nurse was able to murder babies at a Chester neonatal unity over a two-year period

Lucy Letby was moved from the neonatal unit to administrative duties in July 2016 after consultants expressed concerns about her to the hospital’s executive team.

Hospital bosses opted to carry out a number of reviews into the increased mortality in 2015 and 2016, but did not invite Cheshire Constabulary to investigate until May 2017, as Letby remained on site until her arrest more than a year later.

Continue reading...
title: Lucy Letby public inquiry report findings to be published after repeated delays – latest updates

author: Graeme Wearden
description:
Wage growth – used to set triple-lock pension – slows to 3.9%, meaning state pension should hit £13,000 next year

  • ‘Costing billions’: is the pensions triple lock a lifeline or simply unaffordable?

If the state pension rises to £13,000 next year, it will probably breach the UK’s tax-free personal allowance (currently £12,570) – the amount you can earn before paying income tax.

However, pensioners who don’t receive any other income should still be exempt from paying tax if the state pension exceeds the personal allowance.

In the 2025 Budget the government announced the personal allowance would be frozen at its current level up to April 2031.

It also announced that p
title: Pensioners are ‘big winners’ with triple-lock set to rise by 3.9%, lifting state pension to £13,000 – business live

description:
Comments come after court on Monday rejected the president’s mail ballot restrictions ahead of the November midterm elections

  • Supreme court rejects Trump’s mail ballot restrictions for midterm elections

Donald Trump is facing a rare backlash from the US Congress as Democrats and some Republicans push for guardrails on the world’s most powerful AI companies.

Concerns over the dangerous potential of AI reached fever pitch this week after tech leaders sounded the alarm over the rapid advancement of the technology and its potential threat to humanity.

Mitch McConnell, the 84-year-old former Senate majority leader from Kentucky, was seen in Washington for the first time in months on Monday, minutes before his office released a statement saying
title: Democrats say supreme court rejection of Trump mail ballot restrictions will ensure ‘safe, secure and accurate elections’ – US politics live

author: Caitlin Cassidy
description:
Councillors say locals have been raising concerns about people secretly filming in change rooms, swimming pools and around schools

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

One of Sydney’s largest councils has joined the City of Brisbane and the City of Yarra to issue a ban on AI smart glasses at public pools as concerns mount over the potential for predators to exploit the new technology.

On Tuesday evening, Canterbury-Bankstown voted overwhelmingly in favour of banning the tech at its pools, with its mayor, Bilal El-Hayek, describing them as “pervert glasses”.
title: One of Sydney’s largest councils joins ban on ‘pervert’ glasses at local swimming pools

author: Julia Kollewe
description:
Overall grocery inflation jumps to 2.3%, as Ocado and Lidl gain market share

  • Business live – latest updates

Parents and carers spent 12.5% less on school uniform in the run-up to the start of this academic year, turning to promotions and second-hand items to keep expenses down as families struggled with the cost of living crisis.

The average spend on school uniform was £54.53 in the four weeks to 6 September, down an eighth from £62.29 in the same period last year, according to the market research company Worldpanel by Numerator. Overall grocery inflation picked up to 2.3% from 2.1%.

Continue reading...<
title: Parents seek out school uniform deals, cutting average spend to £54.53

author: Lauren Cochrane
description:
More than 1,200 people including Ben Fogle sign letter saying buying British will help preserve manufacturing firms

  • Business live – latest updates

London fashion week is only days away, but one industry organisation has turned its attention to clothing that is a little less catwalk-worthy – the uniforms worn by British defence forces and NHS staff.

On Wednesday afternoon, the thinktank Fashion Roundtable will hand deliver a letter to No 10 urging Andy Burnham to commit to manufacturing these uniforms in the UK.

Continue reading...
title: Make NHS and MoD uniforms in UK, fashion firms urge Burnham

author: Jakub Krupa
description:
Danish PM says action was ‘reckless’ as Moscow-attributed security incidents continue to intensify across Europe

Separately, Dutch authorities are investigating a major outage that affected parts of the country’s railway system, suspecting a possible sabotage after objects were placed on tracks.

The objects caused failures across the network, affecting several level crossings which ‌disrupted road traffic, Dutch rail infrastructure operator Pro Rail said ​in a statement.

Continue reading...
title: Denmark summons Russia’s ambassador after warship fires flares at Danish army helicopter – Europe live

author: Alex Daniel
description:
Labour should replace levy in 2027 rather than 2030 as energy bills are poised to surge over the winter, says lobby group

The North Sea oil and gas industry has called on Labour to scrap the windfall tax on fossil fuel firms three years early, as Britain heads into a winter with energy bills expected to reach their highest level since Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.

Offshore Energies UK (OEUK), the industry’s trade body, wants the tax replaced in 2027, rather than in 2030, with a narrower levy that only applies during price spikes.

Continue reading...
title: Scrap windfall tax on oil and gas firms early, North Sea industry urges

author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
description:
Louise Haigh will set out benefits of AI to TUC conference while vowing government will take safety seriously

Ministers must “heed the warnings” from industry leaders about the threat posed by AI as it looks to capitalise on the technology, the first secretary, Louise Haigh, will say on Tuesday.

Labour MPs and peers have called for the government to further cooperate with international partners to build regulation for the technology, after three Anthropic researchers warned that artificial intelligence could kill off humanity within the decade.

Continue reading...
title: UK must heed warnings from AI experts, minister says

author: Julia Kollewe
description:
Carmaker builds on relationship with British armed forces by seeking to cash in on Europe’s rearmament drive

  • Business live – latest updates

Jaguar Land Rover is in talks with Nato countries about selling them the newly revamped Defender military vehicle, as the UK-based carmaker seeks to tap into Europe’s defence spending boom.

It is also among carmakers bidding for a UK defence ministry contract worth £900m to replace an ageing fleet of Land Rovers that have been out of production since 2016, competing with General Motors and the UK’s Ineos.
title: Jaguar Land Rover in talks to sell Defender to Nato countries

author: Amanda Meade Media correspondent
description:
Witness tells court he sent Jones friendly messages after two alleged assaults because he had been generous to him

  • Listen to the podcast Alan Jones on Trial

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A prominent athlete who has accused Alan Jones of twice kissing him without consent has told a Sydney court he continued to text the broadcaster after the alleged assaults because Jones was powerful and had been generous to him.

The witness, who is appearing for a second day in the seventh week of a lengthy trial, agreed he had sent Jones friendly messages after the two alleged assaults.
title: ‘I was being polite’: prominent athlete continued texting Alan Jones after alleged assaults due to his reputation, trial hears

description:

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Fugitive property developer Jean Nassif has declared he cannot be silenced as he ranted about “crook” politicians and proclaimed his innocence during an expletive-laden tirade at the New South Wales anti-corruption watchdog.

Nassif, 58, on Tuesday dialled into the Independent Commission Against Co

author: Libby Brooks
description:
In today’s newsletter: Plaid Cymru, the SNP and Sinn Féin have signed an agreement for greater powers, as pressure grows on Westminster over the UK’s future

Good morning. Back in May, the shape of British politics shifted dramatically. I’ll forgive you if you were too preoccupied refreshing Andrew Sparrow’s live blog for the latest speculation about Keir Starmer to notice, but since 7 May, centre-left nationalist parties that ultimately aspire to leave the UK have been in government for the first time simultaneously in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.

This week sees the initial codification of that shift. In Cardiff yesterday, Plaid Cymru leader Rhun ap Iorwerth, Scottish National party leader John Swinney and Sinn Féin vice-president Michelle O’Neill (who shares power with the Democratic Unionist party) affirmed their countries’ right to seek independence from the UK. Along with the leader of the opposition in Ireland, Mary Lou McDonald, they signed a memorandum o
title: Tuesday briefing: How to understand Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland’s joint call for change

author: Sarah Basford Canales
description:
One Nation leader had been condemned by figures from across the political spectrum over the newly resurfaced podcast comments

Pauline Hanson has made a qualified apology after describing Indigenous Australians as the “most primitive race on Earth”, saying she did not intend to upset people and said she was sorry “if I offended people”.

The One Nation leader has been under fire from all sides of the political spectrum after the comments from a podcast in September 2025 resurfaced.

Continue reading...
title: Pauline Hanson says she’s sorry ‘if I offended people’ with Indigenous Australians remarks

author: Nick Visser with AAP
description:
Stefanovic agrees to purchase shares from joint owner of 123 Podcast with fledgling show on hiatus since August after Tommy Robinson interview

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Former Today host Karl Stefanovic has cited an “irreconcilable breakdown” in dealings with his business partner as the New South Wales supreme court weighs how best to divvy up their holdings in a fledgling podcast.

The relationship between the long-time face of Nine’s flagship Today program an
title: Karl Stefanovic to buy out podcast partner Keshnee Ibrahim after ‘irreconcilable breakdown’, court hears

author: Nino Bucci
description:
NT police say the person ‘unlawfully gained access’ to the base in the suburb of Winnellie

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

An intruder remains on the run after allegedly forcing their way on to a Royal Australian Air Force base in Darwin, assaulting a member of the defence forces and fleeing in a stolen car.

Defence confirmed in a statement that on Monday afternoon a person “unlawfully gained access” to the base in the suburb of Winnellie.
title: Intruder on the run after allegedly breaking into RAAF base in Darwin and assaulting defence force member

author: Phillip Inman
description:
Economists urge John Healey to press Bank to change policy that is costing the exchequer billions of pounds

Economists have urged the chancellor, John Healey, to press the Bank of England to slow down its bond-selling programme that has already cost the exchequer billions of pounds.

The Bank’s monetary policy committee (MPC) meets this week to not only decide the level of interest rates but also whether they should freeze or slow the sale of government bonds, known as gilts, bought as part of the rescue operation after the 2008 banking crash.

Continue reading...
title: Bank of England urged to slow or halt bond-selling to slash UK borrowing costs

author: Caitlin Cassidy and Australian Associated Press
description:
James Vlassakis was 18 when he became involved in the Snowtown killings, later pleading guilty to four of the 11 murders

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The youngest person jailed over the notorious Snowtown killings will walk free after serving a 26-year sentence behind bars.

A decision to release James Vlassakis by South Australia’s Parole Board was upheld by the Parole Administrative Review Commissioner on Tuesday.
title: Youngest Snowtown murderer to walk free from jail after 26-year sentence as parole upheld

author: Associated Press
description:
Decision allows states to send ballots under process followed for years even as president tried to limit system

The supreme court on Monday rejected Donald Trump’s mail ballot restrictions for now, capping a flurry of last-minute legal action with voting in the midterm elections already underway.

The decision allows states to continue sending out mail ballots under the same processes they have used for years.

Continue reading...
title: Supreme court rejects Trump’s mail ballot restrictions for midterm elections
